channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Quaest: para 60% dos eleitores, partido do candidato influencia escolha de voto para presidente
item.description: A Quaest poll reveals that 60% of Brazilian voters say the candidate's party influences their presidential vote choice, with 38% stating it influences a lot and 22% saying it influences a little. Among independent voters (those not identifying with Lula, non-Lulist left, Bolsonaro, or non-Bolsonarist right), 50% say the party does not influence their vote, while 47% of Lulists and 48% of Bolsonarists say the party influences their choice a lot. The survey interviewed 2,004 people from August 10–13, with a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Bolsonaro vira alma penada da sucessão presidencial de 2026
item.description: Despite being barred from political acts and social media, Jair Bolsonaro was the focal point of the first day of the 2026 election campaign. His symbolic presence, described as that of a 'wandering soul,' haunted venues like Vila Euclides stadium and Copacabana beach, even without appearing in person. The text emphasizes that neither Lula nor Flávio Bolsonaro were the protagonists of the campaign’s opening day.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro tentam inflamar suas bases antes da disputa pelo eleitor de centro
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro launched their 2026 pre-campaigns by returning to their political strongholds to energize their bases: Lula in São Bernardo do Campo, invoking his union roots and historical legacy, and Flávio in Copacabana, reinforcing bolsonarist identity. Both aimed to rekindle militant enthusiasm before targeting centrist voters, using emotional symbolism and historical references to solidify internal support. Lula’s event emphasized past and present government achievements, though with little novelty, focusing on reinforcing PT identity and contrasting his administration with Bolsonaro’s.

item.title: ‘Hoje, até Lula me pediria para permanecer no Senado’, diz Marina Silva
item.description: Marina Silva, former Environment Minister and ex-senator from Acre, announced her candidacy for the Senate from São Paulo, stating she intends to serve the full term and that President Lula, if re-elected, would ask her to stay in the Senate due to the environmental agenda being at risk in Congress. She criticizes recent congressional changes to environmental licensing and the enforcement against illegal mining equipment, arguing that, had she been a senator, these measures would not have passed in their current form.

item.title: Marçal, Garotinho, Arruda: entenda por que candidatos inelegíveis ou com pendências conseguiram registrar candidatura
item.description: Candidates with judicial impediments or ineligibility, such as Pablo Marçal, Anthony Garotinho, Arthur Henrique, and José Roberto Arruda, managed to register their candidacies with the TSE, but their registrations remain under review by the Electoral Justice. Registration is merely the first procedural step and does not guarantee the right to run, as the TSE must still verify compliance with legal requirements. The TSE will assess each case after the August 15 registration deadline.

item.title: Remo desafia o Internacional em duelo na zona de rebaixamento
item.description: Internacional and Remo face off in the Brasileirão 2026 relegation zone, with Colorado needing to end a six-match winless streak. Remo, in 18th place, seeks its first away point against an Internacional side that last won 4-1 over Vasco in May. Betting odds favor Internacional (1.55), with strong likelihood of both teams scoring (1.91), based on recent head-to-head history.

item.title: Entenda o que são estrelas vermelhas e bandeira do Brasil no Instagram
item.description: On Sunday (August 16), supporters of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) used emojis in Instagram's 'Notes' feature to show support in the 2022 elections. Lula's backers posted a golden star on a red background, referencing the PT flag, while Flávio's supporters used the Brazilian flag, associated with Jair Bolsonaro. Some also shared a funk containing offensive content against Lula.

item.title: TRE-DF defere primeira candidatura ao GDF
item.description: The TRE-DF approved the candidacy of Professor Robson (PSTU) for the Government of the Federal District, following a ruling by Judge André Puppin. The decision confirms that the candidate met all legal requirements for registration. This is Robson Raymundo da Silva’s second run for the GDF, having previously contested in 2022 and run for the Federal Senate in 2010, 2014, and 2018.

item.title: Mau tempo cancela agenda de Flávio Bolsonaro em Juiz de Fora
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled his participation in a motorcycle rally in Juiz de Fora on Monday (17) after adverse weather conditions prevented his flight from Rio de Janeiro from taking off, specifically due to 'ceiling' restrictions. His campaign staff confirmed the cancellation, attributing it solely to poor weather. The event was part of his presidential campaign agenda.

item.title: Estreia esvaziada sem Michelle e Nikolas provoca críticas no PL e abre discussão sobre formato dos atos de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's debut street rally in Copacabana drew around 9,000 attendees, significantly fewer than the crowds mobilized by his father Jair Bolsonaro in past events, sparking internal criticism within the PL over the event's format. Despite the low physical turnout, the live stream reached approximately 35,000 simultaneous viewers, which allies cite as evidence of stronger digital mobilization. PL leadership acknowledges that the large allocated space made the low attendance more visible, suggesting a smaller venue or different location could have avoided the negative perception of emptiness.

item.title: Frozen abre nova era na Disneyland Paris para brasileiros
item.description: Disneyland Paris has become a central destination for Brazilian tourists in 2025, driven by the blend of classic Disney magic with contemporary franchises like Frozen. The park surpassed traditional attractions such as the Colosseum and Vatican in the ranking of most-purchased international tickets by Brazilians, signaling a shift from supplementary stop to primary motivator for European travel. The March 2026 expansion of Disney Adventure World, particularly the World of Frozen area, strengthens this multigenerational appeal by combining nostalgic affection with immersive modern experiences.

item.title: Dino afasta sobrinho de governador do Maranhão do Tribunal de Contas
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the 180-day precautionary removal of Daniel Itapary Brandão, nephew of Maranhão Governor Carlos Brandão, from his positions as councilor and president of the TCE-MA, amid a PF investigation into a suspected criminal organization diverting public funds, including federal parliamentary amendments, and obstructing inquiries. The order bars him from accessing tribunal systems, premises, assets, and contacting individuals linked to the investigation, including the governor and associates.

item.title: Patrimônio de Marçal salta para R$ 7,4 bilhões no registro eleitoral
item.description: The declared assets of Pablo Marçal for his 2026 presidential candidacy, filed with the TSE, amounted to R$ 7.4 billion. However, Marçal himself disputed the figure, telling Estadão that the declaration was incorrect and that he had already requested a correction. He did not disclose what the actual net worth should be.

item.title: TSE reúne mais de 100 diplomatas para explicar segurança das urnas
item.description: The TSE is hosting over 100 diplomats in Brasília to explain the functioning and security of Brazil's electronic voting system, including safeguards against deepfakes and disinformation. Minister Kassio Nunes Marques is presenting the step-by-step voting process and contingency plans for the 2026 elections. The meeting is part of a series since June aimed at reinforcing the transparency and credibility of Brazil's electoral process to the international community.

item.title: Eleição para Câmara dos Deputados terá menos candidatos neste ano
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian Chamber of Deputies elections will feature 7,620 candidates, down from 9,477 in 2022, with lower competition per seat and increased representation of women (37%), college-educated candidates (71%), and indigenous individuals (75). The decline stems from the abolition of party coalitions, the performance clause, and a 2021 election law limiting candidates per party to 100% of state seats plus one.

item.title: Voto em trânsito pode ser pedido até quinta-feira, 20: veja como usar o serviço
item.description: Voters outside their electoral domicile can request absentee voting until Thursday, August 20, to vote in another municipality during the 2026 elections. The request can be submitted online via the TSE’s Electronic Self-Service or in person at electoral offices, with options to select different turns and locations. The allowance permits voting for all offices only if remaining in the same state; in another state, only for president of the Republic.

item.title: Lula e Alcolumbre têm 1º encontro público após reaproximação
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre will meet publicly for the first time since their rapprochement, mediated by Supreme Court ministers. The meeting will take place on Monday, August 17, 2026, in Amapá, where they will visit a Petrobras probe ship in the Equatorial Margin, a region where the state oil company confirmed the presence of hydrocarbons. The encounter is part of efforts to advance stalled government priorities in Congress, including the Security PEC and the end of the 6X1 work scale, aimed at supporting Lula’s bid for an unprecedented fourth term.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja as regras aprovadas pelo TSE para uso de IA durante a campanha
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has established rules for the use of AI in the 2026 elections, requiring clear labeling of AI-generated content and banning its circulation in the 72 hours before and 24 hours after voting. The court also approved reversing the burden of proof in deepfake cases, placing the responsibility on content creators to prove authenticity. AI platforms will not be allowed to recommend or rank candidates, even upon user request.

item.title: TSE manda retirar vídeo de Flávio Bolsonaro que associa Lula ao PCC e ao Comando Vermelho
item.description: The TSE ordered the removal of a video by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro that linked President Lula to the PCC and Comando Vermelho, ruling it as unfounded electoral propaganda ahead of schedule. The decision, made in a virtual plenary with five votes for removal and two against, reversed an earlier rejection by TSE President Nunes Marques, who now voted against keeping the video. The action was initiated by the Brazil of Hope Federation (PT, PCdoB, PV).

item.title: Datafolha divulga na sexta (21) primeira pesquisa da eleição presidencial após início da campanha
item.description: Datafolha will release on Friday (21) the first presidential poll after the official start of the 2026 campaign, based on 2,058 interviews nationwide with a 2-point margin of error. Commissioned by Globo and Folha de S.Paulo, the survey includes all 13 TSE-registered candidates, including Pablo Marçal, whose candidacy remains under judicial review despite being deemed ineligible. Besides the first-round scenario, it will feature four second-round simulations with Lula (PT) and assess candidate rejection, as well as approval and disapproval rates for Lula’s government.

item.title: PF intercepta diálogos de Lulinha com lobista sobre articulações no governo Lula
item.description: The Federal Police intercepted messages between Fábio Luís da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, revealing alleged business articulations within the government, including discussions with the Ministry of Health involving businessman 'Careca do INSS' and a proposed contract for medicinal cannabis in the SUS. The messages also reference meetings with former Lula aides such as Marcola and Berger, and mention Fernando Bittar, Lulinha’s former partner, attempting to leverage Lulinha’s name for deals at Telebras. Lulinha’s defense stated it will not comment on leaked fragments taken out of context, accusing the disclosure of violating judicial secrecy and constructing a distorted narrative.

item.title: Casa Pia x Benfica: onde assistir, horário e escalações
item.description: Casa Pia and Benfica face off on Monday, the 17th, at 4:15 PM Brasília time at the Estádio Municipal de Rio Maior, in the second round of the 2026/27 Liga Portugal. Benfica, under pressure after a 2-2 draw in their opener, aims for their first win with potential returns from Vangelis Pavlidis and Leandro Barreiro, while Casa Pia looks to bounce back from a loss using Henrique Araújo and Rochinha. The match will be broadcast in Brazil on ESPN and Disney+, and in Portugal on Sport TV 1.

item.title: O que pode e o que não pode nas redes sociais durante a campanha eleitoral
item.description: Electoral propaganda has begun, allowing candidates, parties, and federations to present their proposals to voters, but with strict rules established by the TSE, particularly for social media and the internet. It is prohibited to share content that attacks honor, spreads fake news, misuses public resources, or encourages vote-buying. These norms aim to ensure fairness, transparency, and respect for the democratic process during the campaign period.

item.title: Sete em cada dez brasileiros desaprovam uso de inteligência artificial pelos candidatos, aponta pesquisa Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 73% of Brazilians disapprove of candidates using artificial intelligence in the 2026 elections, while only 21% support it. Disapproval is highest among voters over 60 (76%) and lowest among those under 34 (68%). The case involving an AI-generated video of former president Jair Bolsonaro, used at the PL convention to formalize Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy, is under review by the TSE.

item.title: Dos testes ao 'gravando': os bastidores de Fora da Bolha, novo videocast do GLOBO
item.description: The videocast 'Fora da Bolha' by O GLOBO was developed over five months with a team of 15 professionals and premieres every Friday to analyze the 2026 elections. It features Vera Magalhães, Flávia Barbosa, Paulo Celso Pereira, and Thiago Prado, discussing topics such as suspicions involving former Lula aides, Flávio Bolsonaro’s running mate choice, Donald Trump’s influence, and the electoral landscape in Minas Gerais.

item.title: Quaest: para 45%, eleição brasileira corre risco de sofrer interferência estrangeira, e maioria vê direita beneficiada
item.description: According to Quaest poll, 45% of Brazilians believe there is a risk of foreign interference in the 2026 elections, while 48% dismiss the possibility, resulting in a technical tie within the margin of error. Among those who perceive risk, 57% think such interference would benefit the right, largely due to tensions with the United States under Donald Trump, including measures like designating criminal groups as terrorists and revoking diplomatic visas.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro abre campanha escorado na figura do pai
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro launched his presidential campaign at a Copacabana Beach event, emphasizing his father Jair Bolsonaro as the main electoral driver while attempting to distance himself from him. He sought to diminish fear associated with the Bolsonaro name, comparing his father to Pelé, and focused his message on criticizing Lula’s third term, avoiding discussion of his own corruption scandals. Despite resistance from right-wing allies who prefer another candidate, Flávio bets on anti-PT sentiment to build support, though the PT views him as the easiest Bolsonaro to defeat.

item.title: Mensagens de Lulinha sugerem lobby junto ao gabinete de Lula
item.description: Messages exchanged between Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha) and Roberta Luchsinger in March 2024 suggest the duo, under investigation by the Federal Police for influence peddling, engaged in lobbying efforts within President Lula’s office. The material, obtained by the PF and reported by Metrópoles, indicates potential attempts to exert political influence through access to the presidential inner circle.

item.title: TSE recebe embaixadores nesta segunda para defender urna eletrônica
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will host over 100 foreign ambassadors in Brasília this Monday (17) to demonstrate the functioning, security, and transparency of Brazil’s electronic voting system. The session, led by Justice Kassio Nunes Marques, will cover the voting process, contingency plans against deepfakes and disinformation, and details on international observation missions scheduled for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Há quatro anos, Bolsonaro e Lula lançavam suas campanhas para a Presidência; lembre como foram atos
item.description: On August 16, 2022, Jair Bolsonaro and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched their presidential campaigns in Juiz de Fora (MG) and São Bernardo do Campo (SP), respectively. Bolsonaro chose Juiz de Fora — where he was stabbed in 2018 — to deliver a conservative speech with evangelical supporters, attacking the PT and defending private property and opposition to abortion. Lula began his campaign in his political homeland, the ABC Paulista, aiming to reconnect with his working-class and union base.

item.title: Valdemar minimiza público moderado em lançamento da campanha de Flávio
item.description: PL national president Valdemar Costa Neto downplayed the turnout at Flávio Bolsonaro's first presidential campaign event in Copacabana, stating the approximately 8,900 attendees were as expected despite poor weather. The event was monitored by Cebrap's Political Debate Monitor using AI-based P2PNet aerial imaging with a 12% margin of error. Meanwhile, Lula held his campaign opening in São Bernardo do Campo, but no public attendance count was made due to the Presidency's refusal to authorize drone overflights.

item.title: Ainda há tempo de Flávio Bolsonaro se tornar menos detestável que Lula
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election is defined by a contest between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, both facing high rejection, with voters choosing more against one than for the other. The article claims the STF acts authoritatively in favor of Lula, while the U.S. government supports Flávio Bolsonaro through coercive measures, intensifying external polarization. Although Lula currently leads in polls due to lower rejection, the author suggests there is still time for Flávio Bolsonaro to become less detestable than the petista leader.

item.title: Viana cobra explicações sobre mensagens de Lulinha
item.description: Senator Carlos Viana (PSD-MG) demanded explanations regarding messages attributed to Fábio Luís da Silva, known as Lulinha, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation by the Federal Police. Viana highlighted a portion of the conversation in which Roberta claims President Lula is involved in alleged irregularities. The senator shared the excerpt in a post on X (formerly Twitter).

item.title: Ex-presidente do BC abre o bolso e doa R$ 135 mil aos seus "favoritos"
item.description: Former Central Bank president Armínio Fraga donated R$ 135,000 in 2026 to candidates Tabata Amaral (PSB-SP), Marcelo Freixo (PT-RJ), and Felipe Rigoni (PSB-ES), all running for the Chamber of Deputies. Tabata received R$ 100,000, Rigoni R$ 25,000, and Freixo R$ 10,000, continuing a pattern of support seen in 2022 when Fraga donated R$ 1.6 million to 27 candidates.

item.title: Durigan diz que Brasil dá superavit aos EUA e é punido
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said Brazil is being commercially punished by the U.S. despite generating a trade surplus, citing exports of orange juice, coffee, beef, and aircraft assembled with American components. He attributed the situation to the U.S. electoral period, calling it non-structural and expecting trade flows to resume after the elections. Durigan also highlighted the opening of over 600 markets under President Lula and stressed the need for institutional, fiscal, and regulatory stability to attract investments in clean energy, critical minerals, and carbon markets.

item.title: Com pouco a oferecer ao futuro do país, Lula abre campanha olhando para o passado
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign by invoking nostalgic memories of his 1980s unionist past as a factory worker, contrasting it with his current status as a wealthy politician entangled in corruption schemes. While acknowledging the social achievements of his previous governments, the text emphasizes that his legacy includes a historic fiscal crisis, persistent inequality, and alliances with bourgeois parties, leading to scandals like the mensalão and petrolão. The campaign avoids addressing future challenges, instead relying on past rhetoric to deflect from Brazil’s high debt, inflation, and ongoing corruption investigations.

item.title: Ao lado de Alcolumbre, Lula visita navio-sonda da Petrobras no Amapá
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visited Petrobras' drillship in Oiapoque (AP) alongside Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, following the discovery of oil indications in block FZA-M-59 in the Amazon Mouth. Petrobras announced it had identified hydrocarbons in an exploratory well in the Foz do Amazonas sedimentary basin, with production expected to begin within seven years. The visit marks the first joint public appearance between Lula and Alcolumbre after their political rapprochement, emphasizing the economic and social potential of exploration for Amapá and Brazil.

item.title: Eleições na Bahia: o estímulo ao voto Lula-Neto
item.description: The campaign of ACM Neto, candidate for governor of Bahia, has been encouraging voters to support Lula through social media influencers, promoting the idea of a 'Lula-Neto vote' as a strategy to attract petista voters. The subscriber-only article details this tactical political alignment between seemingly opposing campaigns. It highlights the growing influence of social media and influencers in shaping voter opinion in the state.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro retornam à zona de conforto em eleição que será decidida fora dela
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro launched their campaigns by returning to their political strongholds to energize their bases, with Lula in São Bernardo do Campo and Flávio in events aligned with bolsonarismo. Both sought to reaffirm their political identities through emotional and symbolic acts, but acknowledge that the 2026 election will be won by convincing voters outside their comfort zones. Lula emphasized future-oriented proposals such as critical mineral exploration and a new public security approach, while Flávio aims to balance bolsonarist mobilization with the need to attract moderate voters.

item.title: Quaest: 73% desaprovam uso de inteligência artificial nas campanhas dos candidatos
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 73% of voters disapprove of AI use in political campaigns, with only 21% in favor. The backlash intensified after Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign used an AI-generated deepfake of Jair Bolsonaro, which the PT challenged as illegal early campaigning. The TSE has scheduled a meeting on the issue, and Quaest and Datafolha will continue releasing polls through October 3.

item.title: “Torravam a aposentadoria na Europa”, acusa Flávio sobre Lulinha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), presidential candidate, accused Lulinha — son of President Lula — of spending pension funds on expenses in Europe, based on messages exchanged with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation by the Federal Police for suspected influence peddling. The claim was posted on X (formerly Twitter) on Monday, the 17th. The accusation fits into the broader political conflict between opposition and government over alleged privileges and misuse of public resources.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cancela ida a Juiz de Fora por mau tempo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled his scheduled visit to Juiz de Fora (MG) due to adverse weather conditions preventing takeoff from Rio de Janeiro. The location held symbolic significance as the site of his father's 2018 stabbing attack, and Bolsonaro himself had faced a knife threat two days prior. His agenda in Belo Horizonte remains confirmed, including the launch of Flávio Roscoe's Minas Gerais gubernatorial campaign.

item.title: PCB traz Edmilson Costa como candidato à Presidência
item.description: Edmilson Costa, 76, an economist and professor, is the Brazilian Communist Party (PCB) candidate for President in 2026, with Cleusa Santos as his running mate. A native of Pedreiras (MA), he has been active in politics since the 1980s, previously ran for mayor of São Paulo in 2008 and for vice president in 2010. He holds a PhD in economics from Unicamp and serves as the party’s general secretary.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula mantém vantagem de cinco pontos sobre Flávio Bolsonaro na largada
item.description: Lula holds 41% of voting intentions in the first round, five points ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (36%), according to the 10th BTG/Nexus poll. The lead remains unchanged from the previous round. In a potential runoff, Lula leads 47% to 44%, within the margin of error, while 50% of voters reject Flávio and 48% reject Lula, underscoring deep polarization.

item.title: Rede social X muda regras de algoritmo para eleição no Brasil. Entenda
item.description: Social media platform X changed its algorithm to stop recommending accounts and posts of candidates registered with Brazil's TSE during the 2026 electoral period, complying with Resolution No. 23.610/2019. Effective August 16, the change excludes such content from the 'For You' feed, though it remains available on official profiles. X implemented the 'Brazil2026ElectionFilter' to meet the requirement, stating the move aims to reduce unsolicited reach of electoral material.

item.title: O custo da promessa
item.description: The article examines the historical record of fiscal adjustment promises by Brazilian presidents, noting that only Itamar Franco and Fernando Henrique Cardoso delivered sustained primary surpluses, while Lula’s first term partially fulfilled the goal and Dilma, Temer, Bolsonaro, and the current Lula administration failed. The current primary deficit of R$ 157.2 billion over the last 12 months and projected public debt at 83% of GDP in 2026 underscore a persistent structural fiscal challenge despite repeated promises.

item.title: Flávio cancela ida a Juiz de Fora, cidade onde seu pai levou facada em 2018
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) canceled his scheduled visit to Juiz de Fora (MG) for this morning, the city where his father, Jair Bolsonaro, was stabbed during a campaign event in 2018. The reason for the cancellation was not specified in the released information.

item.title: Gabriel Brazão, goleiro do Santos, provoca torcida e comissão do Vasco
item.description: Santos goalkeeper Gabriel Brazão provoked Vasco da Gama’s fans and technical staff after Santos won 3-0 at São Januário in a crucial relegation battle. In a viral video, Brazão celebrated facing the Vasco bench and, when confronted by staff member Ricardo Benarroz, replied sarcastically: 'House? What house?'. Santos eased relegation pressure, while Vasco remains in danger of dropping to Série B.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula antecipou a herança dos filhos?
item.description: O Globo reported that President Lula (PT) may have anticipated the inheritance of his five children over the past four years, which could explain a 35% drop in his declared assets to the TSE. According to the report, Lula told his children he wanted to leave them well off. The story was first published by O Antagonista.

item.title: Brasil garante imunidade a observadores da OEA nas eleições
item.description: The Brazilian government has granted privileges and immunities to OEA election observers for the October 2026 elections, protecting them from arrest, judicial proceedings, and interference with their property and communications. Signed in Washington on August 13, the agreement aims to ensure the mission's independence and will remain in effect until the electoral observation concludes.
